# Multiplexer

`maiman.components.Multiplexer` · category **Passive** · [all components](index.md)

One channel into each port, one fibre out. The transmit end, and a filter.

The complement of the demultiplexer and **not** the same thing as
`maiman.components.Combiner`, which merges whatever it is given. This
filters each input to its own channel first, which is what a real mux does and
is the reason a transmitter tuned to the wrong channel does not simply appear
on the line: it lands on a port whose passband rejects it, and the rejection
is the same number the demux at the far end would apply.

Two inputs carrying a band at the same centre frequency are refused for the
reason `maiman.components.Combiner` refuses them — co-located carriers
interfere and have to be added as fields on a common grid, which is a
different operation with different physics.

## Ports

| Port | Direction | Type |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `in0` | input | optical |
| `in1` | input | optical |
| `in2` | input | optical |
| `in3` | input | optical |
| `out` | output | optical |

## Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Unit | Range | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `first_wavelength` | `1550.0` | nm | 1200.0 … 1700.0 | Channel 0. The rest are stepped from it up in frequency, down in wavelength |
| `spacing` | `100.0` | GHz | 1.0 …  | Channel spacing, in frequency because the grid is |
| `wavelength_spacing` | `0.0` | nm | 0.0 …  | A coarse grid's step in wavelength (CWDM: 20 nm), replacing `spacing`; 0 is off |
| `bandwidth` | `50.0` | GHz | 0.0 …  | 3 dB full width of each channel's passband |
| `order` | `3.0` |  | 1.0 … 10.0 | Super-Gaussian order; 3 to 5 is an AWG |
| `insertion_loss` | `4.0` | dB | 0.0 …  | Loss per channel. An AWG routes, so this does not grow with the count |
| `extinction` | `40.0` | dB | 0.0 …  | Out-of-band rejection floor; 0 disables the floor |

## Constructor arguments

Set when the block is created, not swept: `channels`.
